History: Parthian horsemen from the steppe east of the Caspian took Persia from the Seleucids and built an empire Rome never conquered — Crassus died at Carrhae in 53 BC, and Augustus settled for a frontier on the Euphrates. Parthia ruled Mesopotamia through the whole New Testament period until the Sassanians replaced it in AD 224.
Culture: Parthians were famed mounted archers — the Parthian shot, firing backwards at full gallop — and their kings ruled through vassal lords rather than a centralized bureaucracy.
Religion: Parthians tolerated many faiths across their empire. Zoroastrian tradition was strong in Iran, while Mesopotamian and Greek cults continued in the west.
BibleConnection: Parthians were among the peoples at Pentecost (Acts 2:9), hearing the gospel in their own tongue. Some readers see Parthia behind Revelation's kings from the east (Revelation 16:12), though the text does not name them.
